response: Risk calculators do not accurately predict surgical site occurrences. According to existing predictive models, there is a limited ability to risk-stratify patients and accurately assess the risk of surgical site occurrences (SSO). However, two models, the Veterans Health Administration Risk Stratification (VHRS) and the American College of Surgeons National Surgical Quality Improvement Program (ACS-NSQIP), have demonstrated modest success in identifying patients at risk for surgical site infections (SSI). Further refinement of these models is needed to improve their performance and determine whether modifications to perioperative management based on risk stratification can improve outcomes.
